items.t: Paul Krugman Weighs In on AI Boom and Nvidia's Huang
items.d: Nobel laureate Paul Krugman, a City University of New York Graduate Center professor, argues that stock-market performance should not be confused with the health of the broader economy. Speaking on "Bloomberg The Close," Krugman also says the economy shouldn't depend on one executive when asked about Nvidia's Jensen Huang. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.t: The Economy Can't Be Held Hostage by Nvidia's Huang, Krugman Says
items.d: Nobel laureate Paul Krugman, a City University of New York Graduate Center professor, questions whether President Trump’s reported involvement in Jensen Huang’s reappointment as CEO reflected a “too big to fail” view of Nvidia. He argues that the economy should not depend on a single executive to keep a company stable. He speaks during an interview on "Bloomberg The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

items.t: Huang to Testify Publicly Before Senators Dec. 3
items.d: Bloomberg Opinion columnist Dave Lee said despite Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia, questions remain about the national security risks posed by the Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese Spy and that he hopes lawmakers focus more on where Nvidia chips were sent and what Huang knew, and less on Huang's interpersonal affairs.  (Source: Bloomberg)

items.fullText: Congress Congress reacts with anger and skepticism about Jensen Huang reinstatement Lawmakers on both sides of the aisle vowed to press ahead with investigations into the once-again Nvidia CEO, who’s scheduled to meet with them next week. Elizabeth Warren: Jensen Huang’s reinstatement as Nvidia CEO is ‘shocking’ 21:37 Get more news Live on Share Add NBC News to Google Nov. 23, 2026, 1:37 PM EST / Updated Nov. 23, 2026, 6:19 PM EST By Dareh Gregorian and Brennan Leach The stock market was thrilled with the announcement that Jensen Huang was returning as CEO of Nvidia, but lawmakers on both sides of the aisle reacted with shock — and said they still expect him to answer questions next week on Capitol Hill . “You gotta be kidding me,” Sen. John Cornyn, R-Texas, told MS NOW when he learned of Huang’s reinstatement 11 days after he resigned in the wake of revelations of alleged extramarital affairs, including one with a woman U.S. intelligence believes to be a Chinese spy. In its announcement, the board said it reached the decision after receiving “input from senior levels of the United States government” that his “reinstatement poses no national security risk.” Jensen Huang reinstated as NVIDIA CEO 02:27 “No national security risk? Based on what?” Cornyn asked in a post on X . President Donald Trump told CNBC he’d spoken to the board “directly and indirectly.” “One of the things the board wanted to know, is there a national security problem?” Trump said. “And after a lot of research, we — you know, we’ve been looking at this for more than a couple of days, right? This has been a story for a few weeks. We said no, it’s not a problem.” Lawmakers made clear they still need answers. items.fullText: NVIDIA and Microsoft Expand Accelerated Computing From Azure to Windows PCs NVIDIA and Microsoft expand tools for enterprises to customize AI models and deploy applications across cloud and local infrastructure. November 19, 2026 by Dave Salvator 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! NVIDIA and Microsoft are extending their full-stack collaboration to help organizations build, customize and deploy intelligent applications — from next-generation infrastructure on Azure to industrial systems and Windows PCs. At Microsoft Ignite , the companies are expanding access to Azure virtual machines powered by NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 systems, as well as adding customer availability to NVIDIA open models and customization capabilities through Microsoft Foundry, and new options for running AI at the edge, where businesses generate and use their data. Microsoft is also using NVIDIA technologies to accelerate its own models and services, including NVIDIA Dynamo inference software for post-training and NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs for Bing search models. NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 Running in Azure NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 systems are running in Azure data centers , providing infrastructure designed for demanding reasoning, agentic applications, and large-scale model training and inference. Microsoft and NVIDIA are also collaborating to extend confidential computing to bare-metal and rack-scale AI infrastructure. The work will help protect sensitive models and data while they are being processed, supporting organizations that need to work with proprietary or regulated information. NVIDIA Confidential Computing and attestation help customers verify the computing environment before releasing sensitive models, data or keys. As AI workloads span more interconnected accelerators, the companies are working to extend those protections across the AI factory infrastructure. items.fullText: Ian Buck Kicks Off NVIDIA’s Week at SC26 as Science Enters the Age of Agents At SC26, NVIDIA’s VP of Hyperscale and HPC laid out how researchers can combine simulation, AI and agents to accelerate scientific discovery. November 17, 2026 by Brian Caulfield 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! NVIDIA’s Ian Buck kicked off the company’s week at SC26 in Chicago on Monday with new tools for AI agents, software that can plan experiments, run code and check results on researchers’ own systems. In NVIDIA’s special address, Buck announced Nemotron for Science , the Rubin HPC GPU and an expanded Vera CPU platform for high-performance computing . He also detailed a new collaboration in quantum computing with IBM and Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory . “The frontier of computing and the new scientific stack is going to be simulation, as always, but combined with AI and the future of quantum,” said Buck, vice president of hyperscale and high-performance computing at NVIDIA. Buck opened the talk by looking back to his first public talk on CUDA, at an SC06 tutorial in Tampa, Florida, 20 years ago. NVIDIA now offers more than 1,000 CUDA-X libraries , he said. Open Models for Science Agents “[Agents] have been just a game changer in how we interface with our supercomputers, with our devices, our instruments and how we can do the research,” Buck said. Simulation remains the foundation of scientific computing, “which will always be on the top,” Buck said, with AI, quantum and now agents working alongside it. Nemotron for Science combines the Nemotron 3.5 Super VL open model with a new open chemistry dataset and post-training recipes for life sciences and chemistry, Buck explained. Researchers can run it locally on a DGX Spark, a workstation or their own supercomputer. items.fullText: NVIDIA Expands Slurm to Bring Quantum Computing Into Supercomputing Quantum hardware developers, software providers and supercomputing centers are adopting the community-built Slurm workloads manager and the NVIDIA quantum platform to integrate quantum processors, design future systems and develop scientific applications. November 16, 2026 by Sam Stanwyck 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Quantum processor deployments at supercomputing centers have grown nearly sevenfold over the past five years, with nearly 30 supercomputing centers around the world now in the process of deploying over 50 quantum processors. Many of these centers use Slurm to run scientific supercomputing workloads, so expanding its support for quantum processors builds on familiar workflows and tools, enabling computational chemists, nuclear physicists and materials scientists to bring quantum computing into their research domains without friction. In a new release, Slurm builds on previous work with IBM, Pasqal and the wider quantum computing community to allow QPU builders to create a single interface to their hardware for every supercomputing center, through a simple file. This makes it easier than ever for HPC centers and QPU builders to integrate and serve their hardware. The expansion is already being adopted by Alice & Bob , IBM , IQM , Pasqal , Quantinuum and MQSC and supports the widely used QRMI and QDMI interfaces. Read All NVIDIA Announcements From SC26 Beating the Bottleneck Until now, integrating a QPU into a supercomputing center meant a new software challenge for every new QPU or supercomputing center. By building on existing quantum-HPC interfaces such as QRMI and QDMI, the Slurm expansion allows QPU builders to reuse their integrations across all their deployments. items.fullText: NVIDIA Announces Rubin HPC — A New GPU to Accelerate Agents for Science, Engineering and Analytics A record leap in CUDA cores with accelerated data movement shorten time to results for science and engineering workloads. November 16, 2026 by Dan Ernst 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Announced today at SC26, NVIDIA Rubin HPC is a new GPU in the NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform designed to accelerate simulation and data processing for science, engineering and analytics workflows. As agents help scientists and engineers explore more candidate materials, molecules and designs, they rely on simulations to test those ideas and guide their next steps. Rubin HPC will accelerate those simulations, shortening the path from exploration to scientific discovery and industrial design. The Rubin HPC GPU features a record number of CUDA cores — more than 50,000 on a single GPU — as well as a sparse data acceleration capability that keeps those cores fed with data, and accelerates GPU-to-GPU connectivity with seventh-generation NVIDIA NVLink interconnect technology. Read All NVIDIA Announcements From SC26 Scientists and engineers rely on simulation to understand complex systems before committing to experiments or physical prototypes. Working with agents, these teams can explore more candidate materials, molecules and designs. This increases demand for the GPU-accelerated simulations needed to evaluate those ideas and guide next steps. “For agents tackling science and engineering, faster simulation means faster discovery,” said Ian Buck , vice president of hyperscale and high-performance computing at NVIDIA. “Rubin HPC accelerates the simulations agents use to test ideas and guide their next steps, helping scientists and engineers explore more possibilities and bring breakthroughs closer.” Turning Faster Computation Into Faster Discovery Across climate models, engineering simulations, genomic analysis and financial risk, scientific computing w

items.fullText: AI Day Seoul Brings Together Korea’s Industry Leaders, Startups and Developer Communities November 15, 2026 by NVIDIA Writers 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Over two days at COEX, more than 2,000 attendees converged for AI Day Seoul, bringing together Korea’s industry leaders, startups and developer communities advancing physical AI and AI agents. At the plenary sessions, Deepu Talla, vice president of robotics and edge AI at NVIDIA, said Korea is “punching above its weight,” with Doosan Robotics, Hyundai Motor Group, LG Electronics and SK Group — as well as startups like Real World and Luda Robotics — using NVIDIA platforms to bring general-purpose robotics into the real world. Jonathan Cohen, vice president of applied research at NVIDIA, showed how enterprises can build agents they own and control. Breakout sessions featured speakers from Coupang Intelligent Cloud, Doosan Robotics, LG AI Research, LG Electronics, NAVER Cloud, SK Telecom and Upstage. “It was a genuinely enjoyable time to have candid conversations,” said Hyunho Yang, research engineer for omnimodal foundation models at SK Telecom. “Seeing the passion of fellow AI developers was a real source of inspiration for me.” Community leaders share how they build with open models and tools at AI Day Seoul. The Agentic AI 10x Bootcamp Community Day brought together Pseudo Lab, Python Korea, PyTorchKR, HAERAE, Hugging Face KREW, Graph User Group, Womxn Who Code Korea, Dnol (Datayanolja) and other developer communities. Five finalists from the Hangul Day hackathon, co-hosted with Fastcampus, built agents trained on the Korean language and culture with the OpenShell runtime. The winning team, FlyGate, received an NVIDIA DGX Spark system. More than 500 developers also took part in full-day NVIDIA Deep Learning Institute workshops and NVIDIA Certification exams in Korean. items.fullText: AI Is Helping Care Teams Get Patients the Right Care, Sooner Health systems and startups are using the latest AI technologies to support clinicians, streamline workflows and improve patient care. November 13, 2026 by NVIDIA Writers 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! From pediatric research to smart hospitals, AI is helping care teams spend less time on routine tasks and more time with patients. Health systems and startups are putting it to work across healthcare, from matching patients to clinical trials to supporting radiologists, hospital teams and patients at home. Clinicians stay at the center, reviewing AI outputs and guiding decisions, while NVIDIA technologies provide the compute behind the applications. Read on to learn how healthcare teams are using AI to improve and speed patient care. Tuesday, Nov. 17, 8:00 a.m. PT 🔗 Proximie Helps Surgical Teams Spend Less Time on Logistics and More Time With Patients As AI advances healthcare, surgery is a high-stakes, highly regulated setting for its use — and one with significant opportunity for efficiency gains. Only about 10% of time spent in the operating room is clinical. The rest is devoted to scheduling, turnover and documentation. With the help of NVIDIA technology, Proximie is introducing AI into operating room (OR) logistics so that clinicians can focus on taking care of patients. A New Vantage Point Proximie is using NVIDIA Cosmos 3 , the frontier open world foundation model family for physical AI, to power a platform used in more than 700 ORs today. Trained on a decade of data, it captures real-time audio, video and device signals from a close-up view of the surgery as well as a wide view of the whole room. The comprehensive view offers context held by no single person in the room, whether the surgeon, scrub nurse or coordinator. Agentic notifications and voice AI tools can call the next patient when a room is ready, document alerts and capture practitioner notes

items.fullText: 해외소식 삼성전자, 독일서 ‘스마트 사이니지 플립’ 누적 판매 10만 대 달성 독일, 2026/11/09 AUDIO Play Download 공유 레이어 열기 인쇄하기 Google검색에서 선호하는 출처로 추가 삼성전자가 독일 시장에서 인터랙티브 디스플레이 Flip Pro 전자칠판(WMFX 시리즈)가 누적 판매량 10만 대를 달성했다. 삼성전자는 지난 4일(현지시간) 독일 프랑크푸르트 인근 카르벤(Karben)에 위치한 직업교육기관 ‘BBW 쥐트헤센(BBW Südhessen)’에서 기념식을 열고, 10만 번째 Flip Pro 제품을 전달했다. 해당 제품은 4K UHD 터치 디스플레이로, 특수교육기관의 디지털 학습과 직업훈련에 활용될 예정이다. 2018년 처음 출시된 스마트 사이니지 플립은 현재 5세대까지 진화한 삼성전자의 인터랙티브 디스플레이다. 종이 플립차트를 대체하는 디지털 화이트보드에서 출발해 직관적인 사용자 인터페이스와 슬림한 디자인을 바탕으로 교육기관과 기업, 공공기관 등 다양한 분야에서 활용되고 있다. BBW 쥐트헤센은 특수교육 직업훈련과 취업, 자립을 돕는 교육기관이다. 현재 약 500명의 청년이 30개 이상의 직종에서 직업훈련을 받고 있으며, 약 250명이 진로 탐색 프로그램에 참여하고 있다. BBW 쥐트헤센은 수년간 삼성전자 디스플레이를 직업교육과 진로 탐색 프로그램은 물론, 교직원 세미나와 회의 등 다양한 교육·업무 환경에서 활용해 왔다. 이번에 전달된 Flip Pro 전자칠판(WMFX 시리즈)역시 청년들의 직업교육과 디지털 역량 강화를 지원하는 데 활용될 예정이다. 독일 뉴스룸 기사 원문 보기 삼성전자 뉴스룸의 직접 제작한 기사와 이미지는 누구나 자유롭게 사용하실 수 있습니다. 그러나 삼성전자 뉴스룸이 제공받은 일부 기사와 이미지는 사용에 제한이 있습니다. 삼성전자 뉴스룸 콘텐츠 이용에 대한 안내 바로가기 해외소식 더보기 다운로드 닫기 다운로드 할 자료가 없습니다. 본문 복사하기 본문이 복사되었습니다. 공유하기 닫기 페이스북 X 링크드인 카카오톡 메일 라인 복사할 주소 주소복사
